note: The §3 envelope + the limit/overflow/redaction/stale-identity cases. The shape is typed so an unredacted value cannot be represented; the serializer clips bounded lists (most recent kept) and sets truncated: true. The cases below are the pure-logic specification the 73/75 implementations and the serializer test must satisfy.

limits.overflow: the bounded list is clipped (most recent kept) and truncated: true is set — never an unbounded document, never a thrown serializer error

redaction: no absolute paths (data-root-relative or digest/counter only)

cases.result: blocked is clipped to the most recent 100; truncated: true; total ≤ 32 KiB

cases.input: a 500-error flood since the last report
cases.result: errors keeps the last 32 (the ring bound); the rest is dropped, not summarized into unbounded text

cases.input: a code path that would emit a token into a report field
cases.result: unrepresentable by the envelope types; the serializer test rejects it (a defect, caught in CI — not a runtime condition)

cases.input: a consumer cached the report across a backend restart (backendId changed)
cases.result: the consumer MUST re-fetch (the normative stale-identity rule); a cached report is never asserted live; relayed diagnostics whose session/play no longer exist surface the accepted session_not_found / play_not_found

cases.input: a report on a machine without audio/display
cases.result: the report asserts NOTHING about hardware (no capability fields) — the device record is the 67-B/79 surface; the absence is invisible to the report by design
